name: github-workflows-installs
//: The release-tail journey, which installs publish's onevcs from npm, as a project of its own with its own bootstrap, so a change to the rest of the workflow policy, or to the judged-lint toolchain, does not select it. Its inputs name what the journey reads, which is what makes it affected, and then the pull request's affected tier runs it.

test.//registry: llmlint: ignore-block[external_service_suite_stays_out_of_the_affected_tier] this journey reads a public registry with no credential — npm for publish's onevcs, as `just bootstrap` and the gate already reach npm — and it is coverage the base ran on every pull request its inputs reach: moving it to a promoted or credential-gated tier would cut that coverage, which the planner's ruling forbids. Its own project and inputs are what keep any other change from selecting it.
